item.title: SEC fines Tennessee $250K after fans disrupted game vs. LSU by throwing golf balls and mustard
item.description: Tennessee has been fined $250,000 by the Southeastern Conference for fan conduct that disrupted Saturday’s game against LSU, the conference announced Sunday. Fans at Neyland Stadium threw golf balls and mustard onto the field during the fourth quarter of the No. 9 Volunteers’ win over Lane Kiffin’s Tigers , leading the teams to stop play for a few minutes. In a statement, the SEC said that the fine was assessed due to fans “throwing debris” onto the field, interrupting the game and “endangering contest participants.” The SEC appeared to justify the fine with a bylaw referring to the availability of alcohol, saying that the conference can fine the school “if cans or plastic bottles are used as projectiles or otherwise cause game management issues.” The SEC is also able to suspended the university’s ability to sell alcohol at games, though it says that it does not plan to do so at this time. The choice to throw golf balls and mustard was not by coincidence: The seemingly random combination is connected to the school’s previous history with Kiffin. Tennessee’s hatred of the LSU coach stems from Kiffin’s brief stint as head coach of the Vols in 2009, before Kiffin left to coach USC after just one year. In 2021, Kiffin returned to Neyland Stadium for the first time, then coaching Ole Miss. He was greeted with Tennessee fans who threw random debris, including golf balls and a mustard bottle. At SEC media days, Tennessee head coach Josh Heupel encouraged fans to reprise the moment when LSU came to Neyland. “I certainly hope our fan base hasn’t cooled off,” Heupel said at the time. “Whether it’s the grocery stores being fully stocked with mustard, or our sports stores making sure that they’ve got reinforcements on the golf balls, hopefully Knoxville is ready for his arrival.” Volunteers fans happily took the challenge. In addition to bringing the specific items to throw at the LSU bench, several fans also wore mustard bottles in the stands while cheering Tennessee to a 27-13 win. A Tennessee field crew member carries a mustard bottle and golf balls off the field at Neyland Stadium. (Randy Sartin-Imagn Images) IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS Kiffin, for what it’s worth, took the situation in stride. “They listened to their coach,” Kiffin said postgame. “I'm not being critical of him, I'm laughing at it.”

item.description: Mandatory Credit: Mark J. Rebilas-Imagn Images Cardinals’ Mike LaFleur gives Carson Beck injury update after missing Chiefs game appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Arizona Cardinals took the field against the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11. However, they went into this game without rookie Carson Beck under center. Veteran Josh Johnson was the starter on Sunday, with Beck sitting on the sidelines. Beck missed Sunday’s game with a back injury. Johnson took over the offense, but couldn’t lead Arizona to a win. The Chiefs won on Sunday, and Arizona head coach Mike LaFleur spoke about Beck’s injury after the loss . “They’re back spasms. There’s no magic pill you can take for that. You just treat it, and kind of go from there. Obviously kept him back for obvious reasons… We kept Carson back because we didn’t think it was beneficial for anyone to bring him here,” the Cardinals head coach said, via PHNX Cardinals. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Johnson turned in a solid performance for Arizona, tossing one touchdown pass and racking up 155 yards through the air. He did not throw an interception, either. Johnson did fumble once, but it was recovered by the Cardinals. Still, Arizona had no answer for Patrick Mahomes and the Chiefs offense. Mahomes threw for 324 yards while also throwing three touchdown passes. Kansas City improved to 8-2 on the season with its 34-7 victory over the Cardinals on Sunday. Arizona is looking to find some sort of positive momentum in a lost season. One thing that could swing their way is getting Beck back healthy. The Cardinals drafted him in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Seeing what he can do on the field is important for the team’s near- and long-term future. Arizona will look to get back in the win column on November 29 when they take on the Washington Commanders. item.title: Full Card Revealed For ONE Friday Fights 180 On November 27
item.description: ONE Championship closes out November with a fresh slate of martial arts action at Lumpinee Stadium in Bangkok, Thailand, live in Asia primetime on Friday, November 27. ONE Friday Fights 180 features nine bouts across Muay Thai, kickboxing, and MMA, with the athletes chasing the US$100,000 contract and a spot on ONE’s main roster. In the main event, Denkriangkrai Mavinn Muaythai adds another chapter to his long Lumpinee Stadium resume when he meets Myanmar’s Thway Lin Htet in a strawweight Muay Thai contest. The 27-year-old southpaw grew up training at his uncle’s gym, which was built inside a rubber plantation, and he has since become one of the most battle-tested athletes on the weekly series. A former Omnoi Stadium Champion who draws inspiration from his Team Mavinn Muaythai teammate Shadow Mavinn , he owns 10 victories in ONE and is known for a lethal left body kick and a sharp fight IQ. Most recently, he earned a unanimous decision over Abdessamie Rhenimi at ONE Friday Fights 166 . Photo credit: ONE Championship Standing across from him, the 23-year-old Thway Lin Htet is a Lethwei Champion who has built a reputation for highlight-reel finishes. He knocked out Kritpet PK Saenchai with a spinning elbow at ONE Friday Fights 112 and stopped two-time Lumpinee Stadium Muay Thai World Champion Chokpreecha PK Saenchai by second-round TKO at ONE Friday Fights 121 . The Phyo Wai Group representative arrives off a split-decision win over Xavier Gonzalez at ONE Friday Fights 170 , and his forward-marching style and explosive power make him a threat to end any night early. In the co-main event, Nuatoranee Jitmuangnon returns to ONE Friday Fights to take on Yodchanachai Tor Pitakchai in an atomweight Muay Thai bout. The 28-year-old Thai last stepped into the ONE ring at ONE Friday Fights 8 in 2023, and he comes back after more than three years away with a fresh opportunity to make his mark on the weekly series. Yodchanachai, who will be making his ONE debut, will look to make an impression in the opposite corner. Davion Mitchell Should Not Be Underestimated Another player who deserves his flowers after Sunday night’s performance is Heat guard Davion Mitchell . Rivalry Week arrives Friday, Nov. 27, with conference championship implications, postseason positioning and decades of bad blood sharing the spotlight. Georgia has already secured its place in the SEC Championship Game. However, Alabama, Tennessee and Texas still have unfinished business. item.title: Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Justin Herbert enters concussion protocol after Chargers’ Week 11 loss to Jets appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Justin Herbert and the Los Angeles Chargers were sent crashing back to earth after losing to the New York Jets, 27-24 , at SoFi Stadium on Sunday. All the high from the Chargers’ win over the Baltimore Ravens in Week 10 was erased, and it could be more costly, as Herbert was placed in concussion protocol. He played the entire game without exiting for a sideline evaluation. The Chargers have not specified the exact play on which he got hurt. The 28-year-old quarterback did not face the media , as noted by KTLA’s Hayley Elwood. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “Justin Herbert is in the concussion protocol per Chargers PR. He will not be speaking postgame,” wrote Elwood on X. Herbert absorbed significant punishment against the Jets, taking six sacks and eight hits. He suffered a smack to the facemask from David Bailey in the second quarter, which drew a roughing-the-passer call. The two-time Pro Bowler threw 15-of-21 for 131 yards and two touchdowns. He also scored on a short rush to end the first half. The Chargers remained winless at home and fell to 1-9. The Jets, meanwhile, broke their five-game losing streak to the Chargers and improved to 3-8. The much-hyped pairing of Herbert and Mike McDaniel has not worked, and Los Angeles is in danger of missing the playoffs for the second time in four years. If Herbert is unable to clear the concussion protocol before Week 12 against the New England Patriots, DJ Uiagalelei is next in line to start, with Trey Lance out with a groin injury and Jake Browning on the practice squad. item.title: Penguins Get Goalie’d; Play Well, Lose Anway
item.description: DALLAS — Better. Much better, but still not quite good enough. The Pittsburgh Penguins (7-14-2) played their best game in the last handful of offerings, but still had fewer goals on the scoreboard than their opponent, the Dallas Stars (15-6-2). The hockey term is goalie’d as the Penguins had plenty of good scoring chances, but Dallas goalie Jake Oettinger gobbled them up like leftover stuffing after Thanksgiving, and Dallas beat the Penguins 1-0 at American Airlines Arena. The Penguins were significantly better in the first period. The Penguins outshot Dallas 12-11, and the Penguins earned a few glorious chances. A Tommy Novak chance from along the right goal line ended with a miraculous Jake Oettinger save. From nearly the same spot a couple of minutes later, Justin Brazeau hit the post. Midway through the third period, Avery Hayes had a great rip from the slot that was wired for the top corner, but that shot also met Oettinger’s shoulder pads. Rickard Rakell also had a point-blank chance in the final minute, but the Penguins lost anyway. Penguins goalie Arturs Silovs was also quite good. The goal against was unstoppable, but he stopped everything else, and every high-danger chance Dallas threw at him. Egor Chinakhov was also having a game. In the first period, he created a breakaway and then, with a similar defensive stop at the point, launched himself on a one-on-one. However, in all cases, Oettinger made the save. Interestingly, Sidney Crosby had a couple of later third-period shots. He and Chinakhov led the Penguins with four shots on goal. First-period scoring chances: 15-10 Penguins. Second-period chances: 8-2 Dallas. Third-period: 10-2 Penguins. Oettinger was perfect, stopping all 34 shots. Silovs stopped 22 of 23 before being pulled for the extra attacker. Penguins Goal Cap 1-0 Dallas: In a reversal from recent second-period performances, the Penguins were solid. However, good players make good plays. Dallas center Wyatt Johnston turned Penguins D-man Trevor van Riemsdyk inside out at the blue line, and Joel Kiviranta got inside positioning on Kris Letang at the net front. Letang swatted the puck away in anger, but only after Kiviranta (3) deflected Johnston’s hard pass behind Silovs at 12:44 of the second. item.title: 49ers’ Colton McKivitz suffers gruesome injury vs. Vikings
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers have been dealt a devastating injury blow with right tackle Colton McKivitz in the first half of the Week 11 game against the Minnesota Vikings. The injury occurred in the second quarter of the contest and it was immediately clear that the 49ers offensive lineman suffered a gruesome ankle injury. McKivitz came down with the injury when he got his leg trapped under another player. You can check out video of the aftermath of the play in which McKivitz got hurt right here , but warning, it is hard to watch. MORE: DK Metcalf facing suspension after Week 11 ejection vs. Eagles McKivitz stayed down on the field after the play and was tended to by the training staff before being loaded onto a cart and being taken off the field. Players on both teams were obviously very distraught at the site of McKivitz’s gruesome leg injury that is going to keep him out for the rest of the season. The good news is, McKivitz was alert while leaving the field in the cart, but that doesn’t change just how awful it was to see him get injured. MORE: Dak Prescott makes Cowboys history in dominant win over Titans The loss is a tough one for the Niners, as McKivitz is one of the team’s best offensive linemen, and he’s one of the best right tackles in the sport. Entering Week 11, McKivitz was having a phenomenal season with Pro Football Focus grades of 82.8 overall, 71.0 in pass-blocking and 88.8 in run-blocking, ranking seventh, 37th and second among tackles in the NFL. McKivitz didn’t allow a single sack and permitted just 12 pressures in 317 pass-blocking snaps. Vederian Lowe is the next man up for San Francisco, but he will present a significant downgrade for the Niners’ offense. 49ers’ injury woes continue San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan looks on prior to the game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium. Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) No team in the NFL has been as ravaged by injuries as San Francisco this season. Going into the Sunday night game against the Vikings, the 49ers had a whopping 14 players on injured reserve . McKivitz will unfortunately be No. 15. Despite all of their injuries, the Niners have been one of the best teams in the NFL this season. item.title: Weekend Warm-up: Did Bayern Munich do the right thing in signing Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies to massive deals?
item.description: (Photo by Marcel Engelbrecht - firo sportphoto/Getty Images) | Getty Images There is an uncomfortable question hanging over Bayern Munich’s recent contract strategy — did the club make the right investments in Jamal Musiala and Alphonso Davies, or did it allow the fear of losing two exceptional talents to dictate financial decisions that could eventually become difficult to justify? Both players received lucrative, long-term extensions in February 2025. At the time, Bayern Munich vie wed them as essential building blocks for the future. Musiala was arguably the most exciting young attacking talent in German football, while Davies remained one of Eur ope’s most sought-after left-backs. Losing either player, particularly on a free transfer, would have been a significant sporting and financial setback. At the time that each signed, it was reported that neither had a serious suito r. But there was another consideration that could not be ignored — neither player had an entirely clean injury history. Bayern Munich was committing enormous money to two footballers whose availability had already become a recurring concern. Both players received lucrative, long-term extensions in February 2025. At the time, Bayern Munich vie wed them as essential building blocks for the future. Musiala was arguably the most exciting young attacking talent in German football, while Davies remained one of Eur ope’s most sought-after left-backs. Losing either player, particularly on a free transfer, would have been a significant sporting and financial setback. At the time that each signed, it was reported that neither had a serious suito r. But there was another consideration that could not be ignored — neither player had an entirely clean injury history. Bayern Munich was committing enormous money to two footballers whose availability had already become a recurring concern. That concern has become considerably harder to dismiss since the contracts were signed. The numbers from Transfermarkt provide some perspective on why Bayern Munich’s decision deserves scrutiny. Injury prone or bad luck? These figures do not mean either player is destined to remain injury-prone. They do, however, demonstrate that Bayern Munich was not unaware of the availability risks when it committed to these contracts. In Davies’s case, the question about investing that much into the left-back position for a player with that kind of injury track record is likely causing a lot of internal Monday-morning quarterbacking. Per Capology , Musiala’s potential bonuses total €12,450,000. Davies: Up to €20 million per year, including potential bonuses. Per Capology , Davies’ potential bonuses total €5,000,000. Tho se are reported figures, not officially disclosed salaries. There is also a distinction between base salary and performance-related compensation. Capology , which publishes estimated salary data, currently puts Musiala’s gross fixed annual salary at approximately €22.83 million and Davies’s at €15 million, excluding bonuses. As you can see, there are some discrepancies becaus e figures are not publicly released as you might see in North American sports. That distinction between salary and total financial package matters. The headline figures are no t necessarily guaranteed annual payments, and performance incentives can make a significant difference. Musiala’s protection allegedly extends to six months, while Davies’s is reportedly limited to three or four months. Bayern is also said to have taken out additional insurance to mitigate the financial exposure. In other words, Bayern was not simply agreeing to pay two players enormous salaries . It was reportedly agreeing to additional financial protection even if injuries kept them away from the pitch for extended periods. That is a s ubstantial commitment. Why Bayern needed to make the deals There is a very good argument that Bayern could not afford to lose either player in 2025. Mu siala was 21, already a Germany international, and had developed into one of Europe’s most exciting attacking midfielders. He was producin g goals, assists, and moments of individual brilliance while becoming increasingly central to Bayern’s identity. He was also approaching the final year of his previous contract. Bayern needed a player around whom it could build its next generation. Davies presented a different but equally difficult situation. At 24, he was an es tablished Champions League winner with extraordinary pace, athleticism, and experience at the highest level. Losing a playe r of his quality without receiving a transfer fee would have been a significant blow. Finding a comparable replacement would also have req uired a substantial investment. Bayern Munich ultimately secured both players through 2030. That gave the club long-term security, protected the value of two important assets, and avoided the possibility of watching them leave for nothing. There was also a symbolic component. Bayern w anted to demonstrate that it could compete financially with Europe’s wealthiest clubs and retain its most valuable young players. Letting Musiala or Davies w alk would have sent precisely the wrong message. item.title: Fed-up Cal Bears fans curse out players after Stanford rout in Big Game
item.description: Some Cal football fans have had enough. Following the Golden Bears’ rough 44-28 loss in the “Big Game” to their cross-bay rivals Stanford, falling to 3-8 on the season, fans were caught on video cursing out players as they left the field. It’s never good when opposing fans rush the field in your home stadium. But that’s not an excuse for fans cussing out college football players and putting it on the internet. California Golden Bears head coach Tosh Lupoi looks on against the Stanford Cardinal in Berkeley, Calif., Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026. Getty Images But that’s where the Golden Bears find themselves while head coach Tosh Lupoi faces real questions about his job security as an embarrassing season winds down. But Cal hasn’t been competitive for over a month. They haven’t won since knocking off Virginia Tech on Oct. 10, and have lost by an average of 26.2 points over their ongoing five-game losing streak. They’ll look to snap it in their season finale next week when they host Pittsburgh. Virginia head coach Tony Elliott, left, shakes hands with California head coach Tosh Lupoi after a game at Scott Stadium in Charlottesville, Va., Nov. 14, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Cal fans are not happy pic.twitter.com/Okjhl1kiUi — Stuckey (@Stuckey2) November 22, 2026 Lupoi signed a five-year, $22.6 million contract that was finalized in early October, meaning moving on would require Cal to take on a hefty buyout while the school faces a serious budget crisis. Cal’s athletic program reportedly came into the season facing a $24 million deficit and laid off some 20 people in the marketing, athletic communications and creative services departments. Stanford Cardinal players celebrate with the Stanford Axe after defeating the California Golden Bears, Saturday, Nov. 21, 2026, in Berkeley, Calif. Getty Images All while costs have risen during the transition to the Atlantic Coast Conference following the dismantling of the Pac-12 in 2024. Suffice to say, barring something drastic and unforeseen, the feeling coming out of Saturday’s loss to Stanford won’t dissipate anytime soon.

item.title: Coaches Poll Delivers Encouraging Sign for SEC Ahead of Rivalry Week
item.description: Nov 21, 2026; Columbia, South Carolina, USA; Georgia Bulldogs running back Nate Frazier (3) celebrates after scoring a touchdown during the first half against the South Carolina Gamecocks at Williams-Brice Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Jeff Blake-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) ATHENS, Ga. — College football’s coaches have weighed in, and their latest rankings provide another encouraging development for the Southeastern Conference. Georgia maintained the No. 1 position in Sunday’s US LBM Coaches Poll following its 34-6 victory over South Carolina. However, the Bulldogs were hardly the only SEC program making noise. Alabama, Texas and Tennessee climbed in the rankings, while Oklahoma and Missouri returned to the top 25. As a result, nine SEC teams enter Rivalry Week ranked by the coaches. Georgia remains the standard Georgia (10-1) received 60 first-place votes, keeping the Bulldogs ahead of undefeated Utah and one-loss Notre Dame. The Bulldogs have now won four consecutive games, including decisive victories over Ole Miss, Missouri and South Carolina. Meanwhile, Alabama climbed from No. 7 to No. 5, Texas advanced from No. 8 to No. 6 and Tennessee moved from No. 9 to No. 7. Those improvements matter as the conference prepares to determine Georgia’s opponent in Atlanta. Although the coaches poll does not control playoff selections, the rankings reflect the national perception of teams entering the regular season’s final stretch. Complete Coaches Poll Top 25 Rank Team 1 Georgia 2 Utah 3 Notre Dame 4 Miami 5 Alabama 6 Texas 7 Tennessee 8 Wake Forest 9 Texas Tech 10 UCLA 11 BYU 12 Indiana 13 Iowa 14 Oregon 15 USC 16 Arizona 17 Houston 18 Louisville 19 Ole Miss 20 Florida 21 Boise State 22 Oklahoma 23 Missouri 24 Liberty 25 Kentucky One notable difference separates the polls The coaches ranked Alabama fifth, one position ahead of Texas. The AP poll reversed that order, placing Texas fifth and Alabama sixth. Additionally, Kentucky remained in the coaches poll at No. 25 despite dropping out of the AP rankings. Ohio State experienced the opposite situation, falling out of the coaches poll while remaining No. 25 in the AP Top 25. These differences demonstrate how closely voters are evaluating programs with similar records. More importantly, the SEC’s leading teams still have opportunities to influence their postseason positions. Alabama hosts Auburn in the Iron Bowl, Texas visits Texas A&M and Tennessee travels to Vanderbilt. Meanwhile, Georgia closes its regular season against Georgia Tech. item.title: Red Wings trade ex-captain Dylan Larkin to Canadiens in multiplayer and draft-pick deal
item.description: CALGARY, CANADA - OCTOBER 24: Dylan Larkin #71 of the Detroit Red Wings skates against the Calgary Flames during the second period at the Scotiabank Saddledome on October 24, 2026 in Calgary, Canada. (Photo by Brett Holmes/Getty Images) Getty Images DETROIT — The Detroit Red Wings traded ex-captain Dylan Larkin to the Montreal Canadiens in a blockbuster swap involving four players and six draft picks, including two first-round selections, in a deal announced by both teams on Sunday night. In acquiring Larkin, the Red Wings landed forward Kirby Dach, goalie Sam Montembeault and prospect forward Michael Hage as well as Montreal’s first-round picks in 2027 and 2029, plus a 2028 second-round selection and a 2028 fourth-rounder. Along with Larkin, Montreal acquired Detroit’s 2028 second-round pick and a third-round selection in 2027. The long-awaited trade happened between two Atlantic Division rivals and a month after the Red Wings suspended Larkin without pay. The suspension came after the player’s agent informed the team the center would no longer play for the franchise, and had grown frustrated by the Red Wings’ inability to move him months after he asked to be dealt. AP Hockey Writer John Wawrow contributed.

item.title: Player grades: SGA-less Thunder punt in 123-113 loss to Heat
item.description: Eventually scratched from his first game of the season, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander's absence turned this into a skippable watch at worst and background noise at best. The two-time MVP winner went through his pregame warmups, but that was it in his sole visit to one of the most historic gyms in the NBA. The Oklahoma City Thunder stomached through a 123-113 loss to the Miami Heat . They trailed the entire night and by as many as 20 points. Before the cross-conference matchup even happened, the Thunder punted it on the front end of road back-to-back. Not only was Gilgeous-Alexander, but so were Jalen Williams, Chet Holmgren, Cason Wallace, Alex Caruso and plenty of other names. To twist the knife, Aday Mara was a very-late scratch, too. Sure, the Heat were without Giannis Antetokounmpo, but it was a matchup of their B squad butting heads with OKC's C squad. The only Opening Night starter who was suited up for the Thunder was Isaiah Hartenstein. This is the NBA reality they're in right now with their long list of injuries. Any hopes of a miraculous win popped like a balloon. Not even three minutes in, the Thunder were in an 11-2 deficit. Klay Thompson grilled them from the outside — ala 2016. Ajay Mitchell and Jared McCain tried their best collective carry job, but just didn't have the scoring superpowers to do so. The Thunder were in a 36-24 deficit after the first quarter. Finally, the Thunder enjoyed some outside shooting luck. Kenrich Williams drained a 3-pointer to make it a single-digit contest. But anytime it felt like OKC was about to go on a run, the Heat answered back with timely outside jumpers. That was the game's flow throughout the first half. The Thunder had 30 points in the second quarter. They entered halftime with a 67-54 deficit. Bam Adebayo balled out as he flirted with a triple-double. It was the first time this year that he enjoyed first-option hoops. Alas, the second half brought zero intrigue. It was mostly the same as both teams played it out of necessity. Williams had some nice scoring plays, but made costly mistakes as he was asked to be one of their top players. Josh Dix also showed flashes as OKC's best two-way guy with outside makes and good defensive energy. Mitchell had an epic four-point play. But yeah, that's really it. We're really grasping at straws to find meaty thoughts on this inevitable loss once Gilgeous-Alexander was ruled out. The Thunder had 26 points in the third quarter, but the Heat continued to stiff-arm them on the scoreboard. At that juncture in the game, OKC was in a 95-80 hole. Remember when it had a several-year run as one of the league's top defenses? If you stayed through this, you're a real NBA trooper. Enjoy whatever online brownie points you can get. The skeleton Thunder gave you every incentive to tune into the NFL Sunday slate instead. The fourth quarter was forgettable as the game got out of hand. OKC put up 33 points in the final frame to pretty up the final score of this wire-to-wire defeat.

item.title: César Azpilicueta: ‘At Chelsea a draw was a catastrophe – if you can’t perform, you’re out’
item.description: Former defender reflects on his record-breaking longevity, kicking Eden Hazard in training, and life after retirement César Azpilicueta looks well. César Azpilicueta always looks well – “ah, Captain Handsome,” one Chelsea fan says when told who’s turning up – but today especially, smiling in the sunshine. Strolling in, he eases into an easier chair, golf course spreading out beyond the terrace, west of Madrid, and orders a detox almost as green. It is nearly 20 years since he played his first game and a few months since he played his last, training kit replaced by bermudas, loafers and a polo, a picture of relaxation. So what’s it like not being a footballer? “Well, different,” he says. Then he laughs, which he does a lot. It is not a laugh-your-head-off laugh, more a chuckle, a giggle, as if amused at everything he did. And for all the self-deprecation, the lack of triumphalism, he did everything. Now, at 37, it’s not the same, although there remains much to do, Azpilicueta as understated and quietly busy as ever: “square,” he calls himself. He’s completed an MBA, a sports directorship diploma and there are media offers, a life to live. Matches to play still: against his kids the needle is never far away, he says. And although he hasn’t found a seven-a-side team yet he will. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
item.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly coached by Daniel Farke and up to sixth after two clinical strikes from Noah Okafor, Calvert-Lewin’s sixth goal of the season and a late effort from Brenden Aaronson, were so dominant that they had no real need for a helping hand from the officials. item.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
item.description: For Aston Villa , a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago. Villa were too predictable, short of a spark, someone to unpick an organised back line. Johan Manzambi, Emi Buendía and Alysson all flattered to deceive on an afternoon when Ibrahim Mbaye and McGinn arrived from the bench. Alejandro Garnacho, however, was not involved in Villa’s matchday squad for the second successive match and the Chelsea loanee has played just 38 minutes in the Premier League this campaign. Tammy Abraham, the match-winner in April, was also left out and a January move looks likely. Continue reading...

item.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
item.description: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row. Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in Coventry’s favour. With five minutes remaining, a long throw arced into the box. Brandon Thomas-Asante headed it goalwards. Dean Henderson got in the way but the ball bounced off him, hit Dwight McNeil and ricocheted in. “We came through with spirit,” Lampard said. “There was good play and a big impact from the subs. It’s a good sign for the squad.” Continue reading...

item.title: What history tells us about the Premier League table after 10 games of a season
item.description: Past years suggest it is tough to make big positional gains after slow start but that someone now safe will be relegated The Premier League is about to enter the most intense phase of its season. After 10 rounds of fixtures across the past three months there are 10 in the next seven weeks. Yet if you hibernated for winter, most clubs would be in roughly the same position no matter when in spring you emerged. Across the past decade, Premier League teams’ positions changed by an average of 2.6 places between matchweeks 10 and 38. Only 5.5 clubs per season moved by more than three places over the final 28 games, with almost half of the teams (89 out of 200) shifting by a single spot at most. Every club other than Arsenal will be looking to improve their position but they need not trouble themselves too much. History shows they will probably finish 2026-27 close to their current standing. item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Reliving the drama: England and Argentina stars watch 1986 classic with fresh eyes
item.description: A new film about the historic World Cup quarter-final clash finds new angles for a new generation “Is there anything new to say about it?” Gary Lineker asked the producer Flora Fernandez-Marengo when she first approached him to take part in The Match, a documentary about the 1986 World Cup quarter-final between England and Argentina. Flora told an audience at the London film festival premiere of the film that she played her best card then and showed Lineker an image of Maradona with Queen in 1981, during the band’s tour of Argentina. Maradona wearing a union jack T-shirt and Freddie Mercury an Argentina strip. It worked. Lineker said yes. The rock’n’roll angle, with Brian May as a talking head, is one of the very few details the film-makers added to Andrés Burgo’s book, The Match, on which the documentary is based. The directors Juan Cabral and Santiago Franco play with the timeline, hopping between past and present across 91 minutes, the exact duration of the match itself. Anecdotes that now form part of Argentina’s football folklore are spliced with excellent archive material. Continue reading...

item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. This is an extract from Soccer Desk, a newsletter from the Guardian US. Subscribe for free here . Have a question for Jonathan? item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
